newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower on US attack, rate report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower on US attack, rate report.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen interest rate futures closed lower on Tuesday as news that the United States had launched a cruise missile attack against Iraq sent the dollar higher and reminded traders of the yen's fall against the dollar when Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990.
Market sentiment was already weak in the early afternoon by a newspaper report that a bigger-than-expected rise in U.S. interest rates is possible in the near future, traders said.

The Wall Street Journal reported in its Tuesday edition that U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers were mulling a bigger-than-expected interest rate increase unless clear signs of slower growth emerge in the next three weeks.
The Fed could act as soon as its next policy meeting on September 24 after analysing key economic data, including employment and inflation indicators, the WSJ said.

"Unlike the forex market, it took a while before the Euroyen futures market started to react to reports on the U.S. attacks on Iraq," said a city bank dealer. "The market eased firstly on the Wall Street Journal's report."

But long-liquidation was accelerated in Euroyen futures soon after the Pentagon said the U.S. military had launched cruise missile strikes against air defence targets in Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds.

"Operators followed what they learned from the past," said a trust bank dealer. Those who had gone long closed their positions on anticipation of a weak yen because the dollar and U.S. short-term interest rates were driven higher when U.S.-Iraq tension arose before the Gulf War, he said.
After the March fell below the 99.11 support point, further selling pushed it down to slightly above 99.05, traders said.
The contract's low was 99.06. Earlier in the day, it rose to 99.17 in the morning, buoyed by a brief fall of the Nikkei stock average below the critical 20,000 level.
The ongoing December ended down 0.05 at 99.23 in turnover of 68,018 contracts. Turnover of the March was 89,636.

Cash money rates moved little after the Bank of Japan maintained its neutral stance in the money market this morning, traders said. The key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.47 percent, unchanged from Monday's weighted average.
The sell quote for key three-month certificates of deposit was 0.53 percent, the same as on Monday.
